SCL.
Ponraj vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
ORDER The first accused in S.T.No.1126 of 1993 on the files of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kalpetta, has filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (h) (j) and Section 7 (i) and 16 (1) (a)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w Rule 5 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

entities.text:
Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kalpetta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 6 packets of sweets totally having a weight of 200 gram from the first accused on 2.3.1993 at 11 a.m.
After sampling as per law, one sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst submitted Ext.P4 report stating that the sample contained a non-permitted coaltar dye namely Rhodamine B. and was therefore adulterated under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.

Ext.P12 report of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample contained a non-permitted coaltar dye namely Rhodamine B. and hence it contravened Rule 28 of the P.F.A. Rules and was therefore adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P28 were marked for the prosecution.
No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P4 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act .

Therefore, Ext. P4 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case as adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).
A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.

In the said circumstances, the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below cannot be Ponraj vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89510806/
2 sustained.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (h) (j) and Section 7 (i) and 16 (1)
(a) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w Rule 5 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioner stands cancelled and he is set at liberty.
